page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-144 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 288 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 156262.69 and a Passmark CPU score of 134972.44, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50%. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8), which significantly accelerate vector and matrix operations. This is reflected in top-tier Geekbench ray tracing and Passmark extended instructions scores.

The memory subsystem exhibits high throughput, achieving a cached read bandwidth of 11546.73 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 543.81 GB/sec. This high memory bandwidth supports intensive data processing tasks, as evidenced by top-tier performance in Redis SET operations (207.26 million operations per second) and static web serving throughput (216.99 GB/sec). Additionally, the hardware demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds for smaller models drop to average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-144 offers high compute density and specialized instruction sets, making it highly efficient for parallel processing workloads without the added cost of GPU hardware. However, the lack of local storage and a relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio represent clear tradeoffs for memory-bound databases or local-storage-heavy applications. This instance is best suited for high-performance computing (HPC), software compilation, large-scale web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
